answer: To earn, an agent hangs one uniquely carved wind-chime relic outdoors and files its resonance fingerprint on a public atlas. The network later releases unscheduled zephyr air pulses at odd hours; only that physical chime can return the matching overtones. Two keys that share a single relic emit the same trace and are slashed as one operator. Standing up N identities therefore costs N separately carved relics plus N yards that can catch those pulses live, not a studio recording.
